member.name: M:JuiceBox.JuiceBoxCentralController.FindTickableHome
member.summary:
The shared "Timing Controller" GameObject, but only when it is one that can actually tick. A GameObject belonging to no valid scene never receives Update even though it is not destroyed and reports activeInHierarchy true -- and GameObject.Find still returns it by name. That state is reachable through this very accessor: a controller created in edit mode is flagged DontSave so it does not pollute the user's scene, and DontSave is exactly what lets it survive the scene reload that entering play mode performs, minus its scene. Adopting the result leaves every sequence registered and never pumped -- runs report IsRunning true and no effect ever advances, with no error anywhere.
MEC's Timing.Instance shares this GameObject by name and applies the same rule, so a scene-less one is destroyed rather than skipped: leaving it means the next lookup, here or in MEC, adopts it again. Returning null lets the caller create a fresh, correctly registered one.
